title: Conspiracy m4d (x12b picture, 59.100 s): music +12 dB over m2 from frame 0, intro levelled, tick highs cut, word-speed sidechain, folder close 2
notes: m4d: audio-only variant of m2. Liam on m3b (+6 dB): music still way too quiet; start it at the beginning of the scene; lower the very high, whistly sounds. m4c and m4d differ only in music.extra_db (m4c +9, m4d +12 dB over m2 under speech: cue at -29.3 / -26.3 LUFS); the pause opening stays +5 dB above that; ducking timing as m2.

Start: m2 entered the cue at bar 3 (track 3.252 s) at scene 5.519 s, so the first 5.5 s had no music. m4 moves the cue 4 bars (one 4-bar phrase, 6.22 s of scene) earlier so it is already playing at frame 0 (track 3.95 s, 0.72 s after the bar 3 downbeat; bar 4 lands at 0.87 s) with a 0.1 s fade-in; a downbeat still lands on both anchor frames: bar 17 on the CENSORED? landing (f632, 21.0667) and bar 41 at 58.40 (m2: bars 13 and 37). Speed from the two measured onsets (1.0152, +26 cents; m2 1.0159).

Intro: the cue's opening (bars 1-12, track 0-19 s) is quieter than its body (3 s short-term median about 3 dB lower, dips 5-6 dB at bars 3-4 and 7-8); an upward-only slow leveller (music.level_intro) lifts it toward the body's median short-term loudness, max +8 dB, ramping out over the bar before bar 13; the body is not touched.

Highs: the 'whistly' sound is the clock-tick transients' top band, 12-17.2 kHz (rising to a tonal peak at 16.8 kHz, brick-walled above 17.2 kHz), 7-10 dB per Hz above the 4-9 kHz region and alone in the mix (the dialogue stops at about 8.5 kHz); nothing tonal stands out in 4-10 kHz. Cut: high shelf 6 kHz -6 dB, second high shelf 11 kHz -8 dB (so about -14 dB above 13 kHz), notch 16.8 kHz -6 dB Q 8; applied before the -18 LUFS normalisation, so the level targets hold on the filtered cue. High-pass 100 Hz as m2.
Everything else (effects, folder close 2, stamps -2 dB, the end fade, -16 LUFS / <= -1.3 dBTP) as m2.
